Compare pooled peptide-level HDX uptake across states without matching peptides

Source: R/compare_states_unmatched.R
compare_states_unmatched.Rd

A deliberately different tool from compare_states_tp(): instead of requiring the same peptide to be identified in every state being compared, this pools every peptide in a chosen residue range within each state into one distribution, and asks whether that region's typical exchange level differs between states - no peptide correspondence required at all. Useful when peptide identification differs enough between states (chimeras, point mutants, differently-digested runs) that peptide-matched comparison would discard too much data, at the cost of a real confound: two states can appear to differ purely because their peptide maps differ (different lengths/boundaries), not because the underlying exchange does. See Details.

Usage

compare_states_unmatched(
  filepath,
  times,
  regions,
  states = NULL,
  value = c("raw", "percent", "frac_deut"),
  method = c("peptide", "classic", "resample"),
  reference = NULL,
  replicates = 3,
  pvalue = 0.01,
  alpha = 0.01,
  p_adjust = "none",
  n_perm = 1000,
  n_boot = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  p_adjust_method
)

Arguments

filepath

filepath to the input file (read via all_data_long_input() - no peptide matching between states happens at any stage).

times

a single Deut.Time value to compare at.

regions

required named list of c(start, end) residue ranges, e.g. list(NTR = c(1, 85), ACD = c(86, 165)) - see Details for why whole-protein pooling isn't offered.

states

character vector of states to compare. Default NULL uses every state found in filepath.

value

one of "raw" (default), "percent", "frac_deut" - which column drives the comparison. See "What gets compared: value".

method

one of "peptide" (default), "classic", "resample" - see Details.

reference

optional state name - if given, only reference vs. each other state is tested, instead of every pair.

replicates

not used: every replicate of every state is used. Kept so that older calls still work.

pvalue

significance cutoff. This function does not compute is_sig for the pooled shift_hl/p_value result itself (callers can filter p_adj < pvalue there themselves), but pvalue does gate the per-peptide frac_peptides_significant diagnostic - see "Pooled significance is not peptide significance". Default 0.01.

alpha

alpha of the pooled Hageman & Weis critical interval used by the per-peptide diagnostic. Default 0.01.

p_adjust

multiple-testing correction passed to stats::p.adjust(): "none" (default) or e.g. "BH", applied across every region-by-pair test together, and, for the per-peptide diagnostic, across the peptides of each pair of states.

n_perm

number of label permutations for method = "resample". Default 1000.

n_boot

number of bootstrap resamples for method = "resample"'s confidence interval. Default 1000.

seed

optional random seed for method = "resample", making the permutation p-values and bootstrap interval reproducible. The caller's own random-number stream is left unchanged. Default NULL.

p_adjust_method

deprecated; earlier versions used p_adjust_method = "BH" by default. Supplying it sets p_adjust, with a warning.

Value

a list with value (the value argument actually used, echoed back for plotting/labeling) and three data.frames: summary (one row per region-by-state-pair: region, state1, state2, n1, n2, shift_hl, ci_low, ci_high - NA unless method = "resample" - p_value, p_omnibus, p_adj, n_peptides_tested, n_peptides_significant, frac_peptides_significant - see "Pooled significance is not peptide significance"), coverage (one row per region-by-state: n_peptides, mean_length, and frac_shared_all_states - the fraction of that region's peptide identities, by Start/End/Sequence, present in every state being compared, a diagnostic for how much the matched-vs-unmatched confound applies here), and data (the pooled deut_value values the tests actually ran on - one row per region-by-state-by-peptide, or per replicate under method = "classic" - for plotting with plot_compare_states_unmatched()), and peptides (the matched per-peptide results behind the diagnostic: delta, p_value, p_adj, ci and significant per region, pair and peptide).

This is exploratory, not confirmatory

Unlike compare_states_tp(), results here are shift_hl/ci_low/ ci_high/p_value - deliberately not is_sig/delta - so this function's output is never mistaken for the package's confirmatory Hageman & Weis criterion. Always inspect the returned coverage table before trusting a result: if frac_shared_all_states is low for a region, the states' peptide maps differ enough there that some of any observed shift may reflect peptide composition, not biology.

Why regions is required

Pooling every peptide in the whole protein mixes a strongly bimodal mix of protected-core and exposed-loop behavior; the pooled median is then governed mostly by which peptides happened to be identified (composition has more sequence available in exposed regions to fully deuterate), not by biology. Restricting to one structurally coherent region at a time keeps the pooled distribution closer to unimodal and interpretable.

Read the per-peptide diagnostic first

summary lists the matched per-peptide diagnostic first (n_peptides_tested, n_peptides_significant, frac_peptides_significant), then the pooled region test. The pooled test is approximate: it treats the region's peptides as independent samples although overlapping peptides share residues, and it compares peptide means without their replicate variance. For peptides measured in every state, compare_regions() (a two-way ANOVA with peptide as a block) is the more powerful region-level test.

Pooled significance is not peptide significance

The pooled test above answers "does this region's typical exchange shift" - it says nothing about whether some peptides in the region shift while others don't. A real, spatially localized effect (e.g. a binding interface covering a handful of peptides inside an otherwise unaffected 200-residue domain) gets averaged against every unaffected peptide riding along in the same region and can come back completely non-significant even though individual peptides in it clearly differ. To surface this, summary also reports n_peptides_tested, n_peptides_significant, and frac_peptides_significant: for every peptide identity (Start, End, Charge and Sequence - each charge state counts as its own peptide) shared between that pair's two states in that region, a per-peptide matched Welch t-test (replicates of that one peptide, state1 vs. state2 - the same kind of test compare_states_tp() and plot_fissure_vent() use), with p-values adjusted across the peptides of each pair of states, and called significant when p_adj < pvalue and the difference exceeds the critical interval. A region with a flat/non-significant pooled result but frac_peptides_significant > 0 means real, localized signal exists in there - shrink regions to isolate it, or use peptide-matched testing directly instead of pooling.

What gets compared

value: filepath's raw # Deut column (Da uptake, read as X..Deut) is used directly by default (value = "raw") - no per-peptide size correction of any kind. Two other options exist, off by default:

"raw"

Default. Raw deuterium uptake in Da, exactly the # Deut column from the input file - the most direct reading of the data, and what compare_states_tp()/plot_fissure_vent()/diff_peptides_prep() use as well (their percent = FALSE default).

"percent"

HDX Examiner's own Deut % column - uptake already expressed relative to that peptide's theoretical maximum.

"frac_deut"

This package's own derived metric: # Deut divided by the peptide's number of exchangeable protons (see nb_exch_deut()) - a finer-grained per-residue normalization than "percent". Useful specifically when pooling peptides of very different lengths together in one region and the length difference itself would otherwise dominate the pooled comparison (a longer peptide mechanically carries a larger raw Da value regardless of its intrinsic exchange rate) - trades that off against normalizing away part of the signal, which is why it is opt-in, not the default.

The per-peptide p-values do not depend on this choice (dividing one peptide's two states by the same constant does not change a t-test's p-value), but the critical-interval half of the per-peptide rule and the pooled result (shift_hl/p_value/p_omnibus, which pools values across different peptides) are computed on the chosen scale.

method

"peptide" (default)

Each peptide contributes one value per state (its replicates averaged first). Recommended default - avoids replicate pseudo-replication (replicates of one peptide are not independent draws of "how this state exchanges"). Omnibus: Kruskal-Wallis. Pairwise: Wilcoxon rank-sum, reported alongside the Hodges-Lehmann shift estimate.

"classic"

Pools every replicate row as its own observation (replicates x n_peptides points per state) - reproduces the pooling this package's own prior ad hoc analyses used. Triggers a warning: replicates within a peptide are highly correlated, so this inflates the effective sample size and understates p-values. Kept for reproducing prior results, not recommended for new analyses.

"resample"

Peptide-level like "peptide", but p-values come from a label-permutation test (permuting which peptide belongs to which state and recomputing the test statistic) rather than the Kruskal-Wallis/Wilcoxon asymptotic approximation, and the pairwise shift_hl gets a percentile bootstrap confidence interval (resampling peptides with replacement within each state). Slower (n_perm + n_boot resamples per pair/region); more defensible with small peptide counts per state where the asymptotic tests are unreliable.

See also

compare_states_tp(), all_data_long_input(), residue_level_average(), plot_compare_states_unmatched(), plot_coverage_diagnostics()

Examples

# \donttest{
file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
res <- compare_states_unmatched(file_nm, times = "1800.00s",
                                 regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100), cterm = c(101, 225)))
res$summary
#>   region  state1 state2 n_peptides_tested n_peptides_significant
#> 1  nterm Unbound  bound                 9                      5
#> 2  cterm Unbound  bound                19                      6
#>   frac_peptides_significant n1 n2   shift_hl ci_low ci_high   p_value p_omnibus
#> 1                 0.5555556 11  9 -1.0886667     NA      NA 0.2874954 0.2706274
#> 2                 0.3157895 21 22 -0.3056667     NA      NA 0.5762709 0.5680073
#>       p_adj
#> 1 0.2874954
#> 2 0.5762709
res$coverage
#>   region   state n_peptides mean_length frac_shared_all_states
#> 1  nterm Unbound         11    15.72727              0.8181818
#> 2  nterm   bound          9    14.22222              0.8181818
#> 3  cterm Unbound         21    12.33333              0.8695652
#> 4  cterm   bound         22    12.09091              0.8695652
# }
